subject: Renewal: capacity flexibility + tranche credit proposal and floor pricing
messages:
From: rohan.mehta@redwood.com
To: claire@archeon.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: capacity flexibility + tranche credit proposal and floor pricing

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the candid chat last week about Archeon’s forecasted burst cycles for H2. As discussed, you wanted a renewal that protects against sudden spikes while preserving some upside flexibility. I put together a succinct proposal for how we can handle that without moving you to a larger fixed commit immediately:

Proposal (high level):
- Tranche-based flex credits: a pool of credits that can be applied to bursts above committed usage. Three tranches (small/medium/large) with stepwise pricing.
- Price floor for committed usage: lock current per-token rate for the committed baseline through the 12-month term.
- Conditional top-up discount: if monthly consumption stays within 110% of commit for three consecutive months, we trigger a one-time uplift discount on next invoice.

Attached: a one-page term sheet and your Q1 usage snapshot so you can see where the tranches would have kicked in.

Next steps: If this structure looks like it meets the risk profile, I can convert it into a redlineable term sheet and loop in legal/procurement. Would you like a walkthrough today or tomorrow?

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments:
- archeon_usage_snapshot_q1.csv (CSV, summary of API calls/token usage)
- proposed_tranche_term_sheet.pdf (PDF, draft commercial terms)

From: claire@archeon.ai
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@archeon.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity flexibility + tranche credit proposal and floor pricing

Hi Rohan —

Thanks for the thoughtful approach. This is close to what we had in mind. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop in procurement:

1) How do the tranches price relative to on-demand? I want to be sure we’re not paying a premium for flexibility.
2) Can the credits be used retroactively for a burst that clears our short-term overage within the same invoice period?
3) What are the reporting windows — do you provide near-real-time usage so we can auto-trigger budget alerts?

If you can confirm those, I’ll bring in Sara from procurement and we’ll schedule a short sync. Also — if Marissa wants to weigh in on the concession sizing, happy to take that too.

—Claire
Claire Barnes
Head of Platform, Archeon
claire@archeon.ai

From: rohan.mehta@redwood.com
To: claire@archeon.ai, procurement@archeon.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity flexibility + tranche credit proposal and floor pricing

Claire / Sara —

Thanks for the quick reply. Brief answers below, and I’ve expanded the term sheet to reflect them (see revised PDF attached).

1) Tranche pricing vs on-demand: Tranche rates are set between your committed rate and on-demand. Small tranche is ~5% above commit; medium is ~18% above commit; large is ~30% above commit. This caps the upper-bound cost of bursts while still providing flexibility versus full on-demand.

2) Retroactive application: Yes — credits can be applied retroactively within the same billing period as long as the burst is verified by our usage logs and you submit the request within 7 days of invoice generation. We added the governance steps to the term sheet.

3) Reporting windows: Real-time usage is available via our usage API and the Console; we also provide hourly export and a daily digest. We can add an automated webhook to your monitoring channel.

Operational ask: to keep the concession limited, we propose a tranche pool sized at 25% of your current commit (applied across tranches) with a one-time onboarding credit of 10% of your average monthly bill to offset the first-month spike risk.

If you’re comfortable with that, Marissa and I will draft the commercial redline and loop legal. For transparency, I’m proposing we include the DocuSign link for the 12-month term with the floor pricing and tranche appendix.

Best,
Rohan

Attachments:
- proposed_tranche_term_sheet.pdf (v2 — includes governance & retroactive credit clause)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.com, claire@archeon.ai, procurement@archeon.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: capacity flexibility + tranche credit proposal and floor pricing

Looping in from commercial leadership.

Claire / Sara —

Appreciate the clear framing — I reviewed Rohan’s v2 term sheet. We’re willing to approve the following concession set today:
- Tranche pool = 25% of committed baseline (as proposed)
- One-time onboarding credit = 10% of average monthly spend (applied to first invoice)
- Retroactive credit window = within 7 days of invoice posting, supported by usage logs

Two asks from our side before signature:
1) Archeon signs a usage forecast annex (non-binding) to help sizing future capacity.
2) Quarterly business review cadence for the first two quarters of the renewal.

If those are OK, Ben will prepare the final commercial deck and DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
